title: Scaling on the hard graph
html:
Scaling on the hard graph

Question: Scaling on the hard graph: how does what each society achieves grow with its budget?

Answer: At budgets 750–1500: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budgets 3000–12000: best α = 1, β = 1. Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 24000: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. (Compared at each budget; 8 measures, a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)

  • Budget 750: hardest level: 4.64 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 0.28 against traditional 0.00, clearly better.
  • Budget 1500: hardest level: 6.08 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 1.28 against traditional 0.00, clearly better.
  • Budget 3000: hardest level: 7.48 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 2.80 against traditional 0.00, clearly better.
  • Budget 6000: hardest level: 8.56 against traditional 1.84, clearly better. targets solved: 5.56 against traditional 0.40, clearly better.
  • Budget 12000: hardest level: 9.68 against traditional 5.96, clearly better. targets solved: 8.76 against traditional 3.00, clearly better.
  • Budget 24000: hardest level: 10 against traditional 7.40, clearly better. targets solved: 11 against traditional 5.72, clearly better.

Design (fixed before the run): compared four societies × budgets 750, 1500, 3000, 6000, 12000, 24000 · held the same: a generated idea graph (10 levels × 10 ideas, 2.5 parents each, sequences of 4 bits growing by 3 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, budget 750 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 25 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a generated idea graph (10 levels × 10 ideas, 2.5 parents each, sequences of 4 bits growing by 3 per level, composition 0.7); each run draws its own graph. Only α and β vary. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, a budget of 750 split equally every round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
